Bagmine Insulated Cooler Backpack, 17 Liter Foldable Lunch Backpack with Cooler, Lightweight, Waterproof Thermal Cooler Bag for Picnic, Hiking, Beach, Park, Gray During a rush to haul some foods to a barbecue this past Labor Day, I put some big serving dishes inside. And the space was adequate. It will hold a lot. During that rush, I packed about 3 large Gallon Baggies with loose ice. But, I did notice leakage from the inside to out. Best with ice packs to keep foods and bag dry.

So, I tested it by adding water inside, cleaning it and it does leak. Not 100% leakproof as it claims.

So, don't put loose ice or loose ice in baggies. It will leak. But, I like the idea of using it as a regular little ice chest. And, yes, it will work as a backpack. Often we, in life, may have these day outings, and what a great way to carry cold foods and/or drinks. It does clean up on the outside quite good. Spilled barbecue sauce on it and just wiped it off.

Attractive, doesn't look like a cooler backpack. spacious!

Peltor Soundtrap/Tactical 6-S Electronic Headset, Neckband Style, NRR 19dB My wife and I have owned this model for about five years with no issues from workmanship. These are good reliable active earmuffs and we like the fact we can hear each other well when speaking but it actively blocks loud sounds. However if you are getting these for shooting primarily at indoor shooting ranges you might want to consider something with more than 18dBa protection. We've found that we end up adding foam ear plugs when there are others in an indoor range shooting high caliber firearms, plus if you wear safety glasses (which you should be doing) it can lesson the ability of the cups to form around your ear.
Lastly the changing of batteries is not great. You basically have to take a small flat screwdriver to pry up the ear cups. Over the years my screw driver has slipped and I've poked holes in the actual ear cup foam! And you need to make 100% sure the cover snaps back in completely after swapping batteries else you will be in for a loud surprise when using those the next time, meaning if not sealed properly it will not block as much sound.
I've found that I've put these aside except when I need to hear someone speaking while wearing protecton. Instead I've gone with a simple foam in ear version similar to this model for shooting: https://www.amazon.com/Hamilton-Buhl-NoiseOff-26dB-Black/dp/B01MYUO3ET
text_fidelity_b: Peltor Soundtrap/Tactical 6-S Electronic Headset, Neckband Style, NRR 19dB

TETON Sports Hiker 3700 Ultralight Internal Frame High-Performance Backpack for Hiking, Camping, Travel, and Outdoor Activities; 60L, Red I had originally decided on THIS pack because it was considered an "ultralight" and was only 4 lbs vs 5.. I had done extensive reviews on budget packs and decided on this one. It is OK. I am not a big hiker right now although I am working on heading in that direction. I am a female 5.3 height. I haven't tried to properly fit this on me. But this is my concern about the pack so far: First, out of the gate, the "clip" fastener that fastens the hood of the pack to the body is too small and will not lock in. That needs to be changed out and I need the company to send me a replacement part. I have already notified them about this.. we will see.

The other issue that I originally did not anticipate was going to be a big deal is there are very few pouches on the outside of the pack. The two diagonal zippered pouches on the front are not well designed for holding a lot of stuff. NOW perhaps that design was intentional to keep the weight distribution a certain way. I could see that.. But If you are looking for functionality and organization you pretty much will need to rely on individually bagging your items and arranging them INSIDE the pack. I have watched several packing videos and so I know that there is an art form for doing that .. I have a bit of ADHD and need to make sure I Have a system where i can find things easily. I am concerned that I wll not have enough pouches to keep things organized.. we will see. I know one suggestion is to put different "textures" of bags into the pack to help you find things by feel. Perhaps also have different tags (but that would put more weight in the pack). So I don't know. Not being a hard core hiker I can't tell if this will be the good starting backpack for my needs!. I just at least need to get that new clip for the pack ....

Will update later.

I'm using these on 2 bikes, and have attached them to traditional round-spoke wheels as well as wheels with flat/"bladed" spokes, and they fit both and stay on (haven't had one fly off yet). -smaller than other spoke lights; haven't had problems with them rubbing the fork, brakes, etc. on mountain or road bike

Bad Stuff:
-not as bright; will be visible, but if you want a lot of wattage on the wheel, may need to double-up
-only light the wheel in one direction; thus, a pack of 2 would cover 1 wheel
-no blink mode; just solid-on or solid-off

text_fidelity_a:
Fat Gripz Pro - Special Edition Black (New) (2.25" Outer Diameter) --Preamble--

Like many people, I decided to try out some thick bar grips to optimize my current regimen. I too was attracted by the idea of improving my grip and strengthening the whole complex of muscles/tendons/ligaments in my forearms. So I purchased four kinds of wide bar grips - Fat Gripz One (1.75"), Fat Gripz Pro (2.25"), Iron Bull Strength Alpha Grips (2"), and Yes4All Thick Bar Grips (2.2").

Before the review, some context:

First, you should ease into these things, and so if you aren't accustomed to thick bar grips, I would recommend you start with the Fat Gripz One. I did not do this; I tried to integrate all four into my routine, and as a result I gave myself acute tendonitis in both arms, in the form of Golfer's Elbow. Now I need to take at least 4 weeks off while I heal up, and no one likes that. I don't think this would have been a problem if I just started with the narrower grips and moved up from there.

Second, if use a ruler, my hand is 6 5/8" (168mm) from the bend of the wrist to the tip of my middle finger. The Fat Grips One is fine, the Iron Bull Strength grips are about the limit of decent grip, and the Fat Grips Pro are too large to get my hand around, limiting me to fairly light dumbbells. For pull-ups, only the Fat Grips one are comfortable, the Iron Bull's are marginal. I have chronic issues with my TFCC (something I was hoping to help alleviate through these grips) and the thicker ones tend to aggravate that complex.

Lastly, I am fairly fit. I am about 183lbs (83.2kg) and was doing sets of 23 pull-ups before this. I could maintain those numbers with the narrower wide grips, but with greater effort. I have my pull-up bar (an Iron Gym) wrapped in racket grip tape, so it is about 1.1" in diameter. Most of my dumbbells have bars that are between 1.1 and 1.25" in diameter.

--Product Review--

The Fat Gripz Pros are the gold standard for thick bar grips, and for good reason. These do the best at balancing out material, thickness, grippiness, shape, and cost. While these are a bit too thick for my hands, at least at my current stage of development, I think they serve their purposes well.

---Comfort

The Fat Gripz Pros - which are just the same as their standard grips, but in black - are the most comfortable of the grips I tried, tied with the Fat Gripz One. They aren't soft like silicone grips, but they have a little give to them, making it easier to hold them. Their profile makes them easy to hold - i prefer this flat profile to the curved one found in the Iron Bull Alpha grips. The seam has a bit of a hard edge - it could use a chamfer or bevel - but it isn't too distracting. These will not fit IronMaster dumbbells due to those having a 1.25" bar but fit standard CAP weights and my pull-up bar, which have a ~1.1" bar instead.

---Benefit

These are very wide grips, for me anyway, and so they require a significant change in hand position. I had to drop almost 50% of my reps, and 25% of my weight, in order to use them. This means that I just moved these to my lighter dumbbells - currently they are on 25lbs - where I can use them effectively. A bigger guy likely wouldn't have this problem. However, there was a noticeable benefit to how the exercise felt, in my arms, and visually I noticed the forearms were larger and more toned. I think that there would be a lasting benefit to using these if you integrated it into your routine, with mass gains occurring after a month or so. Once I heal up, I intend to continue using them. They don't rotate as much as grips with harder rubber, but you still may need some contact adhesive to keep them in one orientation, especially during pull-ups.

---Conclusion

While I would recommend the Fat Gripz Ones for beginners, and maybe the Iron Bull Alpha Grips 2.0 for people with hands the size of mine, the touted benefits of these appear to be legitimate. I wouldn't expect immediate, wild results, but adding them to the routine is easy and the cumulative benefits will most likely endure. As such, I would recommend them.
text_fidelity_b: Fat Gripz Pro - Special Edition Black (New) (2.25" Outer Diameter)

text_fidelity_a:
TETON Sports Celsius XXL Sleeping Bag; Great for Family Camping; Free Compression Sack After decades of backpacking with mummy sleeping bags, and never having enough warmth, we transitioned to 4WD tent camping. Although I never really minded the confines of a mummy bag my wife was never crazy about it so we looked for a bag with lots of space, width, and warmth. Weight and bag compression was no longer the primary criteria for purchasing a sleeping bag. That's good because this baby is relatively heavy and doesn't exactly pack small once taken out of the box, but that's fine for 4WD camping.

Experience has taught me that you want to purchase a sleeping bag that is rated at least 20 to 30 degrees colder than the coldest temperatures you expect to encounter. We occasionally camp in the mountains where night time temps drop into the high 20's and low 30's, but most of the time the night time temps are in the 40s to low 70s in a relatively dry Western-US environment, including the high desert. I was concerned we might overheat but my wife and I have remained comfortable across the entire temperature range wearing just a t-shirt and underwear or long underwear. She zips her bag up completely whenever the temps drop into the 40s or lower. I don't think I've zipped mine up completely yet.

We're no longer sleeping on a thin foam pad on the ground. We use these bags on cots with 3" thick foam pads. We both sleep like a rock. Our mummy bags have been handed down to our grown kids. As sleeping bags go, this one is a winner!
text_fidelity_b: TETON Sports Celsius XXL Sleeping Bag; Great for Family Camping; Free Compression Sack

A SLICE RED Packable Backpack Small Waterproof Travel Hiking Daypack I gave the A SLICE RED Ultra Lightweight Packable Backpack (In black) 5 stars as you can see.

Here is my situation. I hunt. Don't find much but I hunt a lot and I have this big professional camo honkering GREAT backpack. I could survive everything but a nuclear war with only that thing. And that's a good thing...but...

I also often hunt out of a portable tree stand and that big old pro back unit is just a mess in that situation. Clunky, And it's heavy! So I was really looking forward to my new backpack for the purpose. I moved the essentials from my pro pack to the new one and it's exactly what I was looking for.

The A SLICE RED Ultra Lightweight Packable Backpack is a baby backpack for sure. It's a dufflebag put together in the shape of a backpack actually. When you get it stuffed it becomes the backpack. It has a front pocket. A mesh side pocket, good for a bottle of water or necessary paper..whatever you like. And the interior, at least for my purposes is plenty roomy. I have room to spare. That surprised me. Unlike the big boys this little pack adds zero weight to whatever you put in there. That's a bonus. The zippers worked fine, btw. Backstraps are adjustable. A little flimsy compared to high dollar, but they don't slip

Is it rough and tumble? Probably not. I wouldn't trust it in rough country with briars and such...but for normal use, it's fine. It is a day hiker or a day hunter. From the cost point and utility it's a fine choice for normal wear. I'm very pleased.
text_fidelity_b: A SLICE RED Packable Backpack Small Waterproof Travel Hiking Daypack

text_fidelity_a: Merit Pro Series Waterproof Case for iPhone 6 Plus/6s Plus - White This is a 4 star build quality case with an extra star for value.  It's very close to a LifeProof (which, at this time, doesn't offer a 6+ case; -- I'd give the LifeProof a 4.25 star build quality) in terms of features.  This case uses a pivot lever to flip the ringer / vibrate switch (careful to make sure you engage the two when you install).  The headphone dongle has metal threads to plastic threads on the case (could cause wear problems down the road).  The charging port door is a definite weaker spot.  On this case it pops open pretty easily.  On my last LifeProof case, this door was the issue when I needed a new phone after going surfing.  My advice:  consider this (or any LifeProof case) as water-resistant, not high-activity waterproof (i.e. good for getting caught in the rain while riding your bike, but not good for surfing or snorkeling).  The charging port accommodates the OEM charging cord, and is a tight fit for Anker, but does not fit the Amazon Basics charger.

text_fidelity_a:
Cilkus Bicycle Pump with Pressure Gauge. Mini Portable Bicycle Pump Compatible with Presta and Schrader Valve Bicycles, Including air Bag Needle and Free Puncture Repair I had a tiny little hand pump and a giant full sized floor pump. I needed something to ride along with my on my bike. So I chose to go with a CO2 canister and this mini floor foot pump. When I saw how small it was, I didn't think it was going to be that effective. Especially with the tires that I'm blowing up. I'm running 26x4 fat tires and there's a lot of volume going on in there. Hopefully, I'll be moving to smaller tubes once I install some tannus armor. In the mean time, I needed more volume than the hand pump could provide and a something more portable than the floor pump.
I tested this out by dropping a tire from 30PSI to 20PSI. The chuck went on solid and locked without issue. The good news is that this pump does move air. The fact that I could see the needle move on the pressure gauge was a good indication of effectiveness. The none gauge version would have been nice for portability, but being able to read pressure on the fly is pretty necessary for me. Also the pump retainer/ foot hold works great for stabilizing the pump.

Things that don't work for me. I don't like that the hose comes out the side. It makes in harder to store.
I would have a like a pressure bleeder valve. And most importantly, the chuck leaks with taking it off. So you have to add more pressure than you planned on and you'd need another gauge that doesn't bleed to read the pressure afterwards.

Overall, while it could use some improvement, it's still a great little tool to have in an emergency. Or even if you want to soften the tires for off road and then pump them back up for the asphalt.
text_fidelity_b: Cilkus Bicycle Pump with Pressure Gauge. Mini Portable Bicycle Pump Compatible with Presta and Schrader Valve Bicycles, Including air Bag Needle and Free Puncture Repair

text_fidelity_a:
(2023 Version) SkatingSpirit Slim Padded Figure Skating Shorts, Hip Tailbone Gel Pad Protective Underwear I usually wear a small in womens, but ordered up to a Medium. It fit like a toddler size. In other words, it did not come close to fitting. So I sized up to an XL and ordered again. It fit. But sadly, the padding -- which I saw on the Medium and fervently hoped would be bigger on the XL -- was still child sized. Adults have more surface area to fall on. These pads were narrow and small, targeting very small areas that one can easily miss during a fall. Also, I barely felt cushioned when I tried gently bumping my tailbone. The hips I didn't feel the padding on at all because I missed no matter how many times I tried falling while aiming for the padding.

The pads' holes are a smart idea to reduce weight, and the idea of breathable cotton shorts with packets sewn on for gel padding is a great idea that gets rid of the hassle of placing akton gel on each spot e.g. the famous skatingsafe gel gear that must be held in place with stinky synthetic tights. But unlike the akton gel, these gel pads, while squishy when pushed with a finger, don't seem to provide the same shock absorption. For now, I will stick to my puffy foam shorts as they provide more noticeabpe protection. I hope this company improves their design and I'd be the first to come back.
text_fidelity_b: (2023 Version) SkatingSpirit Slim Padded Figure Skating Shorts, Hip Tailbone Gel Pad Protective Underwear

Fitbit Inspire 2 Health & Fitness Tracker with a Free 1-Year Fitbit Premium Trial, 24/7 Heart Rate, Black/Rose, One Size (S & L Bands Included) I purchased this model/version because my Charge 4 stopped working after only 2 years of use. The Inspire 2 is a smaller display and, depending on the templates you download on the app, can have more details showing on the home screen. There are a few things that I would complain about but are not major issues: first, there are 2 touch-sensitive nodes on the sides that seem to go off when my wrists are bent back and this happens very often which makes me think the notifications have gone off; the second is that I can’t adjust the vibration intensity on the watch so I miss phone calls and messages many times.

This is still a great buy if you only need the basics. All the features for heart rate, steps, and (this one shows) activity time are what you’re looking for when buying a watch like this.

Fitbit Charge 4 vs Inspire 2: What's the difference?
The Inspire 2 has a plastic body so it's a little cheaper in its appearance compared to the Charge 4. It also has a smaller touchscreen display than the Charge and it has a physical button on the side, making for a less streamlined design than the other two models.

Ultimately, it’s lightweight, compact, and doesn’t use up excessive power like other smartwatches on the market. It also charges pretty fast (20-30 minutes for a full charge) and it takes about 4-5 days to run out of power (2 days for smartwatches). I would definitely recommend that someone to buy it for fitness purposes.

Overall, an economical watch that does the job.

Cons: Fitbits stop working after a couple of years for no reason. This is my 4th one in the last 6 years.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Inspire 2 Health & Fitness Tracker with a Free 1-Year Fitbit Premium Trial, 24/7 Heart Rate, Black/Rose, One Size (S & L Bands Included)

text_fidelity_a:
Burley Design D'Lite 1 and 2 Seat Kids Bike Trailer & Stroller with Seat Recline and Suspension, Old School Blue For context, I bought a 2017 D’Lite two years ago and that has more than 2500 miles on it. I typically ride 3-5 times per week for 10-20 miles each time. We usually ride on paved bike paths, but we have spent some time on gravel on a rails to trails type of path. Despite the heavy use, the trailer has held up really well.

This updated D’Lite has the same frame and overall dimensions as the old model, but the new features make it better than ever. In no particular order, here is what I like about the new model:

The built in front wheel makes the trailer usable as a stroller at a times. The old version could not be freestanding unless it was hooked up to a bike. There were wheel attachments you could buy, but I didn’t want to spend more money on that or carry it around with the trailer. I like how the new version has a front wheel attached to the trailer arm.

The quick release for the trailer arm is way more user friendly. While the old model had a pin with a retaining wire that was hard to open, the new model has a pull pin that couldn’t be easier to use.

The adjustable seat recline is quick and simple to use. Whereas the old version required adjusting a bunch of straps, the new version can be adjusted between three positions with a push of a button.

The cover has more clear, see-through surface area. This makes the inside feel more open and it allows the kids to see more of the outside scenery.

There are now plastic caps over the metal corners. I will no longer scrape or bang my knee or shin on those parts of the trailer while taking it out of the car or setting it up.

My kids like the seats of the new model better than the old one. These have headrests and are easier to adjust compared to the old version.

The frame and cover look to be the same design on the new compared to the old model. I really like the adjustable suspension, and I think it is worth the extra cost to give the kids a smoother ride. Also, I think the suspension makes the trailer easier to pull. And, while I haven’t ridden in the rain yet with this new one, the old design kept my kids dry during wet road conditions and even heavy rain. I have no doubt the new version will do the same sine the cover is the same design.

Overall, I think the updated version is worth the premium over the old version, which was already a really good design to begin with.
text_fidelity_b: Burley Design D'Lite 1 and 2 Seat Kids Bike Trailer & Stroller with Seat Recline and Suspension, Old School Blue

Rukket Sports Glow-Nana Inflatable Lounger, Blow Up & Light Up Air Chair & Couch for Lounging, Camping, Beach, & Festival, Sofa Hammock for Adults & Kids, LED Portable Wind Furniture Loungers This is a really cool product that once I figured out a few tricks to its use I’ve really enjoyed owning.

It will definitely help to watch videos on tips as to the best way to fill these loungers. If you’ve seen commercials showing people quickly swiping these through the air then sealing and sitting down - that is misleading. There must be enough airflow to adequately fill the lounger sack so that will require either a breeze or creating one. This can be accomplished by holding it open and running or, as I do, using a battery operated fan.

This product is different from others in this category as it has a pillow and a light built it with it - both are nice additions. In addition there are pouches on the side perfect for storing a drink, book, sunglasses, etc.

I got the “Glow Galaxy” model when the rechargeable battery powered light is illuminated the lounger glows a cool deep purple color illuminating the star pattern. During the day the light really isn’t noticeable but at night it’s incredible. The thing I’ve found I really like about having the light is when at a festival or on the beach it’s always easy to spot my group based on where my glowing lounger in located.

As with anything like this, air will slowly leak out - the more weight or pressure applied the faster air escapes. If someone drops too hard down on to it more air escapes. None of this is to be unexpected.

Sitting upright we fit 3 of us comfortably side by side although we are all relatively small.

While at first I wasn’t sure if I was going to figure out if I could fill this and seal it without the air escaping, now that I’ve used it for a while it’s really not a big deal. The lounger is comfortable, holds air adequately well and has nice design elements that others don’t. I have had multiple people stop to ask where I got it as it really is quite unique.

This is a cool product that I definitely recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Rukket Sports Glow-Nana Inflatable Lounger, Blow Up & Light Up Air Chair & Couch for Lounging, Camping, Beach, & Festival, Sofa Hammock for Adults & Kids, LED Portable Wind Furniture Loungers

KNOG PWR Modular Bike Light - Device Charging, LED, Programmable Bicycle Light This is a bike light that techies might like more than most bicyclists. The light is modular and you can buy an extra mount for another bike, a spare battery pack or even a higher powered light head if you want. The light is also programmable; you can plug it into your computer via USB and customize the lighting modes or change which modes are available. Are these useful features or gimmicks? You have to decide.

Regarding the main feature of this light, it works very well. The full power 600L mode is very bright in the center and the beam has some width so you can see the sides of the road. The 600L mode gave me about 2 hours of use, which is great for a dark commute. Lower power modes gave me much longer burn times. The price for this light is not bad for the performance (brightness and run time). Some people are turned off by all the gimmick features, but I don't think those add much to the price at all.

I like the twist to activate feature of this light. Most lights use push buttons that can be hard to press when your fingers or wet or cold or when you are wearing gloves. Twist and hold to turn the light on and it returns to your previous mode. Twist quickly to cycle through the modes.

My only real complaint about this light is the handlebar clamp. It is thin plastic. It seems sturdy and replacements are available. However, it has a hinged design with just one small bolt and I could not tighten it enough to keep it rock solid steady when I was riding. That's not a huge problem for a light (as opposed to a camera), but I think this problem could be solved with a better clamp (like the metal 2-bolt clamps that you can buy for GoPro cameras).

Like all Knog products, this light is sleek and stylish. The all metal body looks and feels nice and will hopefully be durable.
text_fidelity_b: KNOG PWR Modular Bike Light - Device Charging, LED, Programmable Bicycle Light

For me, it didn't work - the lanyard just doesn't keep the hydration tube in place. It might corral it, which is useful, but the tube tends to slip within the lanyard with only moderate jostling back and forth.

That would earn it three stars, but the plastic clip broke after maybe a week on the back of my chair - not even along a seam, just across one of the flat jaws. That, and the clip isn't even all that secure - there's no lock that keeps it tight, it just sort of rotates into a closed position and you have to hope it doesn't un-rotate again.

Altogether, would not recommend. The magnetic clip or the spring clips are are a better choice, even if you have to cut a little slot into your insulation sleeve to make it fit.

We have each owned in the past - that kind that looks similar to this, but with that point at the back, which always makes us think, what happens if you land on the back and that point slams the helmet forward...

So when I had the chance to grab this POC Ventral Air MIPS (CPSC) I took it without hesitation. Not only does it look good, but in wearing it, it feels great and gives us a sense of being safer than without a helmet. And for all the helmets we have owned, that this has the blunted back, answers that “what if,”

So this POC Ventral Air MIPS (CPSC) arrived and we broke in right away - had to see it in person. We were blown away by the presentation - it comes in a nice box - make sure to take care of this box, it is your storage box! Inside you’ll find the helmet and a bag. Open up and the helmet goes in the bag in the box - it is a GREAT way to store your helmet! Our previous helmets always end up on a shelf somewhere. This is excellent and we were already impressed.

Next... the helmet. It looks cool. Not only the color - I’m a blue guy and it’s perfect - but the overall design is so cool. We both liked the matted look - over the glossy really - but in person it looks even better. And on, it looks seriously cool. I tried it with both my reading glasses - no point other than to see how well it handles glasses - and my sunglasses - one of several I own, so one design style - and in both cases they fit perfectly under the sides of the helmet. I felt like I could wear them for an hour and have no rub or discomfort. I have not actually worn them out riding yet, but in this situation, the test was impressive.

As to that idea we always wondered about - what happens if you land on the back and that point - this is blunted, meaning there is no point. You land and it makes sense - you’ll have the back side make contact, but in a way that appears it’ll cushion the head and not shove it or the helmet forward.

The helmet is really light weight and you cannot believe how it feels like it could be that light and protect your head. So we put it on... and for me it fit perfectly. I got the large due to my large head. I had to open the strap slightly, but one half turn on the wheel and it was perfect - snug, but not tight nor uncomfortable. Now we only have this one, so when my wife went out to test the scooter, she had to wear this one. She has a much smaller head than mine, but it was nothing to size this down for her - while she technically doesn’t fit their size chart at this size, it worked well - she was comfortable and felt completely secure in it. It was very easy to size down for her, then bring it back up for me. It was easy and quick and we both felt great with it on.

I’ll be honest - this price point is above what we would normally spend. I was able to get it as a Vine Reviewer and for that I am grateful. I normally do not speak to price because of that, but in this case, wish to address it. In talking about it, we WOULD spend the money to get a second one for her. We feel that the safety this “promises” is worth the money. Now that said, We would do much more research first - we are not experts on the safety aspects of helmets and would make sure first. There is NO way we would go out and test this - meaning risk our head to see that is does what it promises. But if our further research shows what we think it would, yes, we would consider spending the money. Brain safety is important and we want something good. Now that said, if there is a product at a lower price that provides equal safety, we would seriously consider that - money is something we are careful with, but so too our safety. In the end, this is an excellent helmet that fits well and comfortably. Safety is the priority. But we do have to be realistic about cost. So if we could afford it and our research indicates it is a value, then yes, we would pay, but if not, if we found something as good at a lower price point, we’d have to look in that direction.

But we both love this POC Ventral Air MIPS (CPSC) helmet and are thrilled to have it.
text_fidelity_b: POC, Ventral Air MIPS Road Cycling Helmet with Performance Cooling

Coleman Evanston Tent Updated Sept 2022. Purchased in 2018:

We use this tent three to five times per year depending on how many people are going. This is a great tent! The instructions on whether or not to use the black poles or the grey poles for the main tent could be clearer, but we wrote that on the bag after setting it up incorrectly twice.

I would not classify this as a three season tent, unless you live in a warmer climate. I live in central Texas, so this will work for me almost year round.

The good :
-very spacious, Large framed door on hinges.
-Good Head room.
-Lots of mesh on roof and two sides.

-Bath-tub floor comes up really high.
-Appears to be good reinforcement at stress points.

The bad :
- Really needs two people to set up (but I suppose if you are buying a tent this large you will have help).
- Stakes. As with any tent now a days, you probably won't be using the stakes that are included.

Buying experience - The tent arrived well before the stated delivery date, and the packaging was in excellent condition.

We now have six tents and three of those are Coleman Tents of various sizes. I have been generally pleased with the products overall, but I do not subject them to harsher environments as I would my Marmot or Eureka.

Warranty - Coleman stepped up and replaced this tent way past the warranty period. We got a rip in one of the sleeves for the main pole. Even though it still sets up OK, we felt it best not to use the tent in case a storm with gusty wing came up (because of the tear).

text_fidelity_a:
PackIt Freezable Utility Cooler, 18 Can, Charcoal Grey The main, cooled compartment is 10.5" x 7.5" x 7" tall. It is a family-sized cooler bag for food or beverages. The gel for cooling is in the front, bottom, and back walls of the cooler. The side walls are just canvas and do not contain gel, and I don't think the top has gel either. The cooler walls can be collapsed so the cooler is flatter and smaller when you place it in the freezer. They recommend cooling it in the freezer for 12 hours before use. There is a zippered, flat outside pocket in the front that is 8.5" wide and 5.5" tall. There is a handle on top of the of the cooler under which is a compartment that will hold things like napkins, phones, utensils, etc. The opening is 5.5" wide. There is no zipper to secure this pocket. Due to the handle being right above the opening for this area, it is not highly convenient to get things in and out. This compartment is about 2" deep and covers the entire width and length of the lid. There is also a zippered, flat outer pocket tucked away on the bottom of the bag. It has an attached pull-out bit of fabric, though I'm not sure what it's for. I'm also not sure what you'd want to place in this pocket, since it's between the ground and the bottom gel wall of the cooler and weight will be on it. The cooler also has an adjustable carry strap. The cooler interior is easy to clean up if there are spills. It seems to be working okay to keep food cool for a few hours while traveling.

This cooler contains polyethylene foam. The advertising says that the "cooler is made from nontoxic poly canvas and has a food-safe, water-resistant lining" and it is made from "...PVC-, BPA-, phthalate-, formaldehyde- and lead-free materials."
text_fidelity_b: PackIt Freezable Utility Cooler, 18 Can, Charcoal Grey

PUTTMON Mate Golf Putting Practice, Indoor Golf Putting Mat with 1/2 Hole Training for Mini Games & Practicing at Home or in The Office, Gifts for Golfers, Golf Accessories for Men My kids and I have been enjoying using this mat, especially with some light up golf balls I recently got. We turn off the lights and practice putting, some times for more than an hour (a very long time for easily distracted 6 and 7 year olds).

The automatic return works well once set up properly, which I had to add more Velcro to keep it flat. Also, the long distance putting doesn’t return the ball straight back, so I’m not exactly sure what that mode is used for practicing. These are my only complaints, but the first was easily addressed and I prefer hitting balls into the holes as that is more satisfying than bouncing a ball off some foam. So neither of these are problems in my mind.

A few notes on where to use this. The automatic return didn’t work on carpet (a medium pile carpet) or an area rug (a pretty firm surface). Also, my basement floor (laminate planks over concrete) is apparently not level in a certain spot. The ball kept breaking to the right, and I first thought the line was printed crooked. But I got my laser level out and I can confirm the lines are straight and they point to the center of each hole. Also, I measured the ramp/box portion with a bubble level and it was level. The box is sturdy (it can withstand a 50 lb kid stepping in it), and it is also pretty quiet with the strategically placed foam. This is a great product, and I highly recommend it.

text_fidelity_a:
Osprey Talon 11 Men's Hiking Backpack , Cosmic Red, Small/Medium Rating is 4.5 stars, see below for why I took 0.5 stars off.

I recently used this backpack over about 10 days of hiking, much of it in hot weather up and down some mountain trails. I wanted comfort: firstly not making my back sticky and hot, and secondly being easy to wear loaded for 6 or more hours in a day. It passed both criteria with flying colors. There are bigger and smaller sizes, so you can get just what you need for your purposes, they should be just as comfortable.

The minor negatives I have are: (1) Ideally there would be a few more small compartments for things like wallets and phones and keys. It's easy to lose things in the depths when small items are packed in with fleece pullovers and jackets and granola bars and such. (2) It's pretty hard to reach back to grab and pull out your water bottles: I ended up working with my travel partner to help each other out for this. I'd prefer a way to set those just a bit forward, and put the little waist packs behind perhaps.

Overall I'm sold on Osprey backpacks, and would buy one again quite happily.

"Weather conditions are a major factor in the wear and tear of the item which is why the instructions sheet states: “Remove when not in use”. Unfortunately, we can not cover these parts under warranty. "

Conquer Indoor Bike Trainer Portable Exercise Bicycle Magnetic Stand This trainer is a very basic, low friction (Light workout) trainer that is very easy to set up.
It is solidly made, and very quick to assemble (really no assembly)
Very nice that it comes with wheel quick release rear wheel skewer to fit the trainer, and front wheel stand.

However, for low noise & a hard enough workout I ended up buying:
> The red trainer tire: Slick for no noise $40
> A shimano cassette that has a tiny 11 tooth high gear $20
> Small 26" tube and rim tape to support the tiny red tire $7

Note: don't make the mistakes of did. I bought a second wheel for $40 to have a quick change from quiet trainer to road-worthy. My bike has a 7 speed Shimano back cassette. The new wheel had a 7 speed Shimano FREEWHEEL WITH 13 teeth high gear. They both work on this bike, but do not share inte changeable cassettes. A "freewheel wheel" is cheaper & weaker- the way the bearings support the axle. (Per good Sheldon brown webpage). And I had to adjust all the derailleur stops to have it shift properly on the freewheel wheel. I needed a 11 teeth high gear to get a good workout, so had to move the red tire & tube to the old wheel with cassettes & get a 11tooth to 28 tooth cassette.

Finally loving my quiet workouts!!!

So, this is a very basic entry level trainer because it has:
> Light drag for the rear tire; just a little magnet drag; no air drag squirrel cage; no flywheel; no fluid drag system. Just a light magnet drag.
> No quick release to get bike on & off; must screw these bolts in & out and fine tune.\
> no quick release for roller pressure on rear tire. Bend down and screw it in trial & error for enough drag without much noise.

About noise:
For me it was a balancing act to get enough of a workout without overtightening the roller which creates a lot of tire squeaking/ deforming noise. I tried tire pressures from around 50 up to the max of 87psi. Still hard to get a lot of trainer drag without slick tire squeaking/ clicking noise.
1. It is not really that the TRAINER that makes any noise at all. It is quiet, but creates very little drag with it's little one-setting magnet.
2. A TIRE with ANY tread will generate noise. Even at a slow low gear for Physical Therapy for an ACL injury, my neighbors were looking over the fence for the strange noise.
3. With a SLICK tire, the noise ranges from near zero (with just enough roller pressure so the tire will not slip on the roller), to "Pretty squeaky/ clicky-noisy" if you press the stainless roller too much more into the tire to increase the workout intensity. The tire simply deforms so much around the roller it has to squeak and slide around, making a pretty loud clicking sound.
Edit: I realized the tire only squeaks loudly a couple mnutes, then gets totally quiet when it warms up. These tire "clicks" sound so mechanical I could have sworn they were coming from inside the roller /drag mechanism. But it's the tire / roller slip that goes away when it gets warmer & stickier.
4. So the actual noise occurs even with a slick tire if you want a hard workout because the stand has very little built in magnetic friction. No flywheel/ no air or fluid drag. So for a light workout it can be quiet. (I'm going to my highest gear on my 21 speed to get more drag)
5. A partial solution for me is to change shimano cassettes and go from a 13 tooth highest gear to a 11 teeth high gear. This makes the wheel spin faster> harder workout> still low enough roller pressure on red trainer tire to be very quiet (only chain & sprocket noise).

I read other reviews saying they wished the bought a better trainer. After a day using this, I understood why. (Low drag on this one, no quick release roller or bike holder, Also, the magnetic drag is sort of a clicky on & off drag ,as if your chain is contributing vibration into your ride; but it's really the magnet drag working properly. So air drag or fluid drive trainers can create a lot more drag without the little clicks, and a flywheel on a better model trainer makes for a more realistic ride feeling
text_fidelity_b: Conquer Indoor Bike Trainer Portable Exercise Bicycle Magnetic Stand

text_fidelity_a:
MOUNTAINTOP Watreproof 3 Season Tents for Camping/2 Person Camping Tent/Backpacking Tents with Carry Bag This tent seems like a great value at first. But when you can't sleep because of water seeping in, then drive yourself mad trying to tear down the tent in the morning you'll regret not buying a real tent.

The only plus I can give to this tent is that it sets up super easily. But to be honest, it's not really that much better than just setting up any other tent. The mechanism they have to pop the tent open works. But you're adding a lot of weight and mechanical complexity to something that's not very difficult in the first place.

On to the negatives.

It's impossibly annoying to tear down. While the tent pops open easily, it's a total pain to close. All of the plastic arms will start popping out of the mechanism. There's 8 joints you need to pull and close, one by one. And then you have to figure out which way the thing actually closes. But there's so much tension in the arms attached to the central hub that if you don't do it just right everything starts popping out.

So instead of just popping your tent poles out of the ground and pulling them out of the tent, you have to tear apart and rebuild this complicated lever mechanism spring loaded hub thing in the middle of the woods. And that's after you got no sleep because there's water in your tent.

The rain fly doesn't cover nearly enough of the tent. So if there's any rain it will rain directly on the tent, where as I said above, water will start seeping through into the tent. not just a little dampness. We had actual puddles in the tent.

I've had $20 Walmart tents that did a better job than this thing. It's not worth the money. It's overly complicated. And worst of all it just doesn't provide adequate shelter.
text_fidelity_b: MOUNTAINTOP Watreproof 3 Season Tents for Camping/2 Person Camping Tent/Backpacking Tents with Carry Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Rayovac SE3DLNBL Sportsman 240 Lumen 3D LED Lantern, Blue After Hurricane Sandy hit the east coast and I was without power for 9 days, I decided to purchase one more light to add to my army of 13 flashlights. I wanted something that would illuminate a room better than my underwater flashlight and my headlamp. My underwater flashlight and head lamp happen to be exceptional lights but they can only be used for focused tasks since they lack a wide range. This lantern not only gives exceptional light but it also illuminates an entire small room.

These are the many features I like:

- The lantern is so bright it is blinding but it definitely lights up my kitchen from 1/2 a room away. I just had to make sure I did not look the light in the eye.
- It has a high and low mode.
- It can also be used as a strobe light (meaning in blinking mode).
- It only takes only 3 D size batteries (only one more battery than most D-battery flashlights).
- It's water resistant.
- It comes with a lifetime warranty.
- The lantern has a tent hook on the bottom; although it is a bit difficult to move.
- It also has an EZ-find light that blinks every few seconds; although that "find" light (which sits above the black power button) is barely visible in the dark.
- Customer service is excellent.

The only problem I had with this light is that it did not come with any instructions; it only comes with a wrap-around paper touting its virtues. Therefore, I had to call the company on the 800 I found on the Internet (you can find that # in my comments) to learn how to make the strobe light work. I also asked how the EZ find light worked because I was unable to detect it.

The tent hook and handle are self-explanatory but to make this light work, this is what I had to do. Please note I executed all these instructions with the front of the lantern facing me:

1. Both the top and bottom of the lantern screw off. The top is where the blub is and that can be screwed off counter-clockwise but there's really no reason to remove the top. I screwed off the bottom clockwise and inserted the 3 D batteries as indicated on the stickers inside. I then lined up the red arrows (both on lid and case) when closing the bottom in the opposite direction I opened it and made I heard it click shut.

2. I pushed the black button to operate the light. Pressing it once brought on high mode and pressing it again brought on low mode. Sometimes I found that after one press no light comes on; in that case I pressed it again until I was in the desired mode. The tech said this was normal behavior.

3. To get the strobe light working, I had to HOLD down the black button for about 5 or 6 seconds until the light started to flash. I then pressed the black button to turn the strobe effect off.

4. To see the EZ find light that is located above the black on off button, I moved the lantern to a totally dark room. This light flashed every 5 or 6 seconds but I still found it hard to see.

In summary, this is a great lantern for illuminating a small room or anywhere I need to illuminate a larger area than a flashlight can provide. The light given off seems fluorescent but it's bright enough to work with. The only thing I did not like is that instructions on how to operate the strobe, insert the batteries, etc. were not provided. Although I was able to figure out how to do most of this, I had no clue I had to HOLD down the on/off button for 5 or 6 seconds to get the strobe feature to work. Since this lantern is going into storage until I need it, I will take out the batteries as the EZ find light will probably drain them after a couple of months.
text_fidelity_b: Rayovac SE3DLNBL Sportsman 240 Lumen 3D LED Lantern, Blue

A friend has one. So this came to mind. I just rest them on each shoulder (I have broad shoulders).

Of the many I researched online, this fit the bill best for higher weight capacity (15lbs total with the 2 on), comfort, looks, price, and staying put on my shoulders.

Fabric is soft but pretty durable, although for true ankle wearing walking I agree with reviews, the fabric would wear down with the heavier weighted ones just due to the fact that a required soft fabric (so not nylon) that’s comfortable on skin must break down with shear, and the heavier the weight the more inherent shear (friction) there’ll be. But, stick to a classic lower weight and that’s not a big issue with these. Go with another that’s more durable and it’ll scratch your skin more. It’s a catch 22.

Anyway, these are great, but particularly for women for whom future osteoporosis could be a thing if you wear them slung over your shoulders.

Wake Bike Stem Riser Bike Fork Stem Extender Bicycle Handlebar Raiser Head Up Adapter Suitable for Mountain Bike, Road Bike, MTB, BMX, Fixie (Aluminium Alloy, Adjustable) This WAKE stem riser comes with enough spacer-rings to put your existing handlebar riser at the right height and allow the stem cap and long stem bolt to fully engage. There was a little difficulty in keeping the alignment of the now top and bottom sections of this taller riser assembly, but I found getting the top on first and clamping it in position so the gaps in top and bottom line up vertically is easier than putting the tall riser on first and then aligning and tightening the top section with the handlebars to it. It can be done either way, but it took a lot of fussing, tightening and loosening and twisting. Getting that long bolt in to press the stem cap down to hold everything in position is complicated that the fork bearing will keep everything loose without the correct alignment, so you have to keep that as a goal because nothing can have a final position without that important fork bearing being seated. Then, all you need to do is clamp it all together on the bike. This is a 2 part operation: the long bolt and stem cap forces the assembled units together and down, then clamping the top and bottom riser sections together and to the bike for a solid steering connection. I think this better than the older-style threaded stem which depends on that single bolt to hold everything in place.
-Compressing in several dimensions makes it more secure.-
The test ride, once I was satisfied that everything had been aligned and tightened, was different from how the bike had been only an hour ago. My hands, arms and shoulders were at a more natural angle and riding was much easier. This riser extension is only 2.7 inches, but coupled with the top riser and raised handlebars the difference is more than 8 inches overall. A nice, comfortable ride!
There are youtube videos showing this operation in detail. //// It's important to do it properly! ////

text_fidelity_a:
YADEA Electric Scooter Adults, Foldable Commuting Electric Scooters KS5, 3 Adjustable Speeds Max 18.6 MPH, 25 Miles Long Range, Dual Shock Absorption, Front Suspension, Triple Brake, Cruise Control I just purchased the KS5 Pro. Here are my comparisons with the KS5.

Larger deck. Both feet fit more comfortably. Heavier. Harder to move around but feels sturdier when riding. Problems with rear fender appear to be solved (see old review). Extra bracing metal stops fender from flopping around like on my KS5. Handlebars are 2-3” higher than the KS5. This is a scooter that should be able to handle 6’6” riders easy…

Max speed drops approx 20% when at two bars and 30% when at one bar. Ex: my max speed when riding in sport mode at one bar is 13-15mph on flats. Max downhill speed is 22mph

My KS5 delivers almost full speed up until one flashing bar...

Max range is about 19 miles.

I weigh 220lbs.

Overall this is a great and sturdy scooter that reduces range anxiety and should be able to get you anywhere within a city.

Note: initially my regen brakes would cut on fully (and seemingly randomly) when I put very light pressure on the brakes. This would happen once for every ~50 times I hit the brakes. This lead to unexpected moments where I would almost get thrown off the scooter. Completely unexpected and super dangerous. I'm very experienced at scootering, skateboarding, biking, and this almost wiped me out each time. This happened for the first week, then suddenly stopped. I had just set the scooter up for return shipping and my last ride (to be completely sure) did not have the problem.

——————-old KS5 review—————-
Update: I’m on my fourth rear fender. They break under normal road vibration. Fracture, crack, break at the base where the fender rises from the deck of the scooter. Four different fenders. No collisions or crashes. This one part needs a redesign.

———————

When the scooter first arrived I was VERY impressed by the build and weight. This thing is a beauty. Ship packaging was adequate with lots of cardboard keeping everything separate and stationary.

Assembly was very simple. Just a few screws to attach and an app to download from the IOS appstore.

Second impression was pretty poor however. Could not get the handlebar post straight - even with max strength. And could not get the headlights to turn on without first using the phone app.

Turns out both were my mistake (and somewhat the fault of the mediocre documentation/startup docs).

You can't access any scooter functions while its charging. So when you first open the box and logically go to charge it, double-tapping to turn on the headlights won't work. You may also need to adjust the screw at the base of the handlebar post. It used a different Allan key size than the included key, but tightening it up a bit will make it easier to open/close.

The app is sufficient. It definitely could use some user interface redesign - its lost opportunity to turn this into an exceptional product - but it suffices for what it is. I set the unit to hi regen on braking and "baby mode" for my first test runs.

Tires are hard. There is some give - but these feel pretty much like solid tires to me. If there is a honeycomb design inside, it will likely show itself on the most heinous road bumps and not by simply pushing a finger or pen into the tire material.

Shocks were pretty sticky when I tested them in my house. Not smooth at all. They loosened up considerably after a 5K test run. And about that test run...

I rode to a smooth track near my house and did about 10 laps. On the perfect surface I was able to focus on the acceleration and handling of the scooter. Very, very good. In S mode has a great pickup, and I achieved MAX speed in a few seconds. Braking was very good. I immediately came to a stop with double as well as single brakes. Regen seemed to bring me to a stop - but was not very aggressive feeling - even on max. That might be due to my weight.

I am a fit 215lbs and am 6' tall. Size 11 feet. The scooter feels like it was built for me. Deck is plenty spacious and handlebar grips are at the perfect height for me. I've been on scooters that felt fragile - this is NOT one of them. I pulled on the bars as I cornered and pushed on them as I braked. No wiggle. No squeek.

After the smooth track, I went to a nearby jacked-up parking lot, filled with cracks, weeds and bumps. The scooter handled 1" lips and 2-3" gaps in pavement well. The shocks did their jobs, but the wheels gave me little joy. I felt significant road vibration. Maybe the wheels need a break in period as well...

As for the weight and storage ... I commute using a folding bike (Dahon Vigor D9) and this scooter weighs significantly more (50%) and is much harder to handle when walking it or when folded. I've gotten into a habit of taking my Dahon with me everywhere possible and I fold it down quickly and roll it around or pick it up when I need to.

This is a bulky scooter and you won't want to pick it up and carry it often. I was able to use it as an unpowered kick scooter pretty easily. So running out of power when on the road should not be a problem. But multimodal commuting might be annoying if you have a lot of stairs to climb or will be on a tight train.

The charge outlet is well-protected with a spring loaded cap. There is also some rubber backing in the cap to help create a better water seal. Should be good for splashes. But I'd stay away from a puddle deep enough to immerse the bottom of the board.

The front and rear lights are very bright. No additional lights are needed.

Changes?

Improve the quality of the app. Make it so good/informative that people will want it open on the handlebar of the scooter while they're riding. Do more quality control of the text as well.

Maybe provide wheels with a tiny bit more cushion. Wheel tech is steadily improving and a softer core wheel (keep it solid) will definitely make folks happier. I can't imagine anyone wanting harder wheels.

Improve your documentation and startup tips card. Larger font. Clearer layout. Put things in order of importance for the best startup experience. A large, colorful startup tips card that says things like (lights won't turn on when charging, adjust handlebar base, etc). And change the screw on the handlebar base to the same size Allan key as the rest of the screws on the scooter. I have tools, some may not.

Excellent scooter and highly recommended!

----------------

Update:

Today I went for a 10 mile ride. I used ECO for 75% and SPORT mode for 25%. MAX speed almost all the way. There were three significant uphills (1/4 mile each) and several large downhills. I used regenerative braking as much as possible. When I got home I had 1 bar left, flashing.

I weight 215 lbs, which is approaching the upper limit of the scooter's spec. So on a full charge I can reliably get about 10 miles out of the scooter judiciously using SPORT mode. For me, this scooter is good since my office is 3 miles away from my house. I can just blast on SPORT both ways.

Since I've owned the scooter the APP has gone through an update adding a few new features. Its still pretty poor quality and does not seem to save my changes to settings like regenerative braking, etc.

------UPDATE-------

I've lowered the star rating by one due to the following issues.

1. Noise. The rear fender makes a LOT of noise when riding. Constant clunking sounds as it flops around. Its very irritating. They also break under the vibration load. I’M ON MY FOURTH REAR FENDER UNDER WARRANTY!!! AND IT JUST BROKE AS WELL. THEY ALL CRACK AND THEN BREAK AT THE SAME SPOT!!!

2. Range anxiety. From a full charge, the scooter drops down to one flashing bar at 8.5 miles on me, regularly. Far short of 25 miles and I'm wistful... It would make sense that the flashing bar is really 25% power remaining instead of 10% or less - but I don't want to test it. I usually need 10 miles of range when I ride the scooter (its a round trip) and I can just eek it out if I only use sport mode for the first 10-20% of my ride (when I need more speed to better negotiate car traffic). By the time I'm heading home using standard mode exclusively I'm stressing range. So I guess I can lose 15 lbs to get better range... Carrying the charger and recharging on the road is not an option in this use case.

3. Accelerator glitches. The scooter has gunned uncontrollably on two occasions. Both times I was sitting at a light, then I pressed the accelerator and the scooter took off at max speed and would not stop, even when I hit the brakes! I had to turn off the power... The first time I thought it was something I did. Second time I realized it was the scooter. VERY dangerous situations for me both times. I can only guess that it may have something to do with cruise control as it did not happen before I turned that on (may be coincidental). I'll turn off cruise control for the time being when riding in traffic/pedestrian settings and will try to replicate the issue in a parking lot and see if its some type of user error...

4. Aftermarket service has been excellent thus far. Yadea have sent me replacement parts for the rear fender. As well as PDF and video instructions on maintenance. Very responsive to requests. Scooter front shocks are still quite sticky. Can’t seem to lube or adjust them to be smoother. Side reflectors are a pain to get off in order to service rear wheel or replace rear fender. However, once you have performed maintenance on the scooter, repeat sessions are easy.
text_fidelity_b: YADEA Electric Scooter Adults, Foldable Commuting Electric Scooters KS5, 3 Adjustable Speeds Max 18.6 MPH, 25 Miles Long Range, Dual Shock Absorption, Front Suspension, Triple Brake, Cruise Control
